sections.title: The Last Supper and the Washing of the Disciples' Feet
observations: In this pivotal moment, Jesus demonstrates humility and servanthood by washing the feet of His disciples. This act is profound, as foot washing was typically reserved for the lowest servant in a household. Jesus, the Master, takes on this role to teach His followers about the nature of true leadership and service.
This act foreshadows the ultimate sacrifice He is about to make on the cross. It illustrates that greatness in the Kingdom of God is defined by serving others, not by exercising authority over them.

sections.title: The Betrayal Foretold
observations: Jesus reveals that one of His disciples will betray Him. This moment is filled with tension as the disciples are troubled and begin to question who it might be. Jesus' knowledge of the betrayal emphasizes His divine foreknowledge and control over the unfolding events.
The act of dipping the bread in the dish with Judas signifies a close relationship, highlighting the tragedy of betrayal from someone so close to Him.

sections.title: A New Commandment
observations: After identifying Judas as the betrayer, Jesus gives a new commandment to His disciples: to love one another as He has loved them. This commandment is central to the Christian faith and sets a standard for how believers are to interact with one another.
The emphasis on love as the distinguishing mark of His followers is crucial. It challenges the disciples to reflect Christ's love in their relationships, which is foundational for the church.

sections.title: Peter's Denial Foretold
observations: Peter boldly declares his loyalty to Jesus, but Jesus predicts Peter's denial. This moment serves as a sobering reminder of human frailty and the need for reliance on God's strength rather than our own.
Peter's denial illustrates the struggle between intention and action, a theme that resonates with many believers as they navigate their faith journeys.

importantVerses.commentary: Jesus washes the disciples' feet, demonstrating the essence of servanthood and love.
A new commandment to love one another as Jesus has loved us, which is foundational for Christian community.

questions: What does Jesus' act of washing the disciples' feet teach us about leadership and service in the church today?
How can we apply the command to love one another in practical ways within our communities?
What does Peter's denial reveal about human nature and our need for grace?
